summary: Michel Soymié (1924–2002) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at INALCO (~1948–1952) and held positions at the CNRS, EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise, EPHE (Chair of Mediaeval China, ~1966–1992), and the Société Asiatique.

Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot University under supervisors including Kaltenmark, Schipper, and Vandermeersch. His posts included UC Berkeley, the University of Bordeaux, and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin.

Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post at the University of Cambridge as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After graduating from the University of Turin (~1853–1857), he taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and held a professorship at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).
Michele Martin (born 1942) is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Queensland (~1996–2000) and taught at Victoria University of Wellington (~2001–2005) and Colorado College.

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his doctoral studies under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998–2002) and held a post at Leiden University (~2003–2014).

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1973). He served at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974–1982) and professor (~1994–2016), and held positions at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute and the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

Michihiko Yajima (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued graduate studies at the University of Tokyo, where he also held a post attested in 1992, and later served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University.

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Setagaya Gakuen High School, Komazawa Junior College as a lecturer, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies as a librarian.

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1978–1983) and joined Western Washington University in 1984 as a professor of foreign languages.

Michio Kamikawa (1960–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1987) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from around 1998 to 2021.

Michio Yano (born 1944) works in Indology and the history of science. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University under David Pingree and Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held positions at Otani University, the Eastern Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student and held subsequent academic affiliations at Tohoku University, with activity attested in 1990 and 2001–2004.
Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held research posts at the Toyo Bunko and the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa.
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where she later held a position as a researcher.
Mieko Kajihara is a scholar of Indology. She studied under Michael Witzel and completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2002.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Miguel de Unamuno (1864–1936) was a Spanish philosopher and writer. He studied at the Universidad Central from around 1880 to 1884 and held a faculty post at the University of Salamanca from around 1891 to 1936.
